items.q: The normal IVC diameter used to determine the amount of fluid required is:
items.exp: Investigations in sepsis-AKI: IVC diameter 2–2.5 cm is normal and determines the amount of fluid required. (Book p800)

items.q: Match each sepsis-AKI parameter with its interpretation — 1) S. lactate >1 mmol/L  2) S. lactate >4 mmol/L  3) IVC diameter 2-2.5 cm … A) Normal value, determining the amount of fluid required  B) Organ hypoperfusion  C) Severe sepsis
items.exp: Investigations in sepsis-AKI: an IVC diameter of 2-2.5 cm is normal and determines the fluid requirement; lactate >1 mmol/L indicates organ hypoperfusion and >4 mmol/L severe sepsis. (Book p800)

items.q: A serum lactate above which value indicates severe sepsis?
items.exp: Serum lactate >4 mmol/L indicates severe sepsis, while >1 mmol/L denotes organ hypoperfusion. (Book p800)

items.q: The passive leg raising test (PLR) is described as:
opts: A test for fluid responsiveness — now obsolete
The investigation of choice for volume status
A test for renal perfusion pressure
items.exp: Passive leg raising test (PLR): a test for fluid responsiveness, marked obsolete in the book, illustrated by the graph with the 30 mL/kg VE fluid challenge. (Book p800)

items.q: Match each sepsis investigation with its purpose — 1) IVC diameter  2) S. Lactate  3) Passive leg raising test … A) Assesses organ hypoperfusion/severe sepsis  B) Determines amount of fluid required  C) Test for fluid responsiveness (obsolete)
items.exp: Sepsis investigations: IVC diameter (normal 2–2.5 cm) determines the amount of fluid required; serum lactate >1 mmol/L = organ hypoperfusion and >4 mmol/L = severe sepsis; PLR tests fluid responsiveness (obsolete). (Book p800)

items.q: A patient in the ICU has a lactate of 5 mmol/L. According to the book this indicates:
items.exp: Serum lactate >4 mmol/L indicates severe sepsis (levels >1 mmol/L indicate organ hypoperfusion). (Book p800)

items.q: The passive leg raising test as a test of fluid responsiveness is described as obsolete.
opts: False — it is the investigation of choice
False — it is a test of renal perfusion
items.exp: PLR is a test for fluid responsiveness, described as obsolete, while IVC diameter and serum lactate remain the listed investigations. (Book p800)

items.q: All but one of the following are listed among the investigations for sepsis-associated AKI. Which is the odd one out?
items.exp: The listed investigations are IVC diameter (2–2.5 cm normal), serum lactate (>1 and >4 mmol/L thresholds) and the passive leg raising test. (Book p800)
